title: fix(workers): bind workspace recovery to its session source
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker workspace recovery can rediscover a different session store after routing changes, redirecting conflict reports or result settlement away from the session that owns the pending work.

## User Impact

Each recovery attempt keeps one exact session source and rechecks its generation and recovery authority. If the source is replaced or authority is revoked, pending results, staged refs, and unfinished journals remain available for a later authorized recovery. Archived sessions can finish retained recovery without becoming active again. Committed destruction still completes its explicit settlement path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing recovery owner prepares the source once and carries it through recovery, conflict reporting, and settlement. Initial row preparation runs in the reader worker. Stable revision checks reuse verified facts; changed revisions compare only the protected owner fields through the existing revision and transcript-write owners, retaining live-authority and before/after revision fences. No stored fields, schema, worker protocol, or dependency changes. Related: #150153.

## Evidence

Before the main refresh, head `774c5ab5ea92782e9279b7fad055f1a8eb9d94ff` passed 67 targeted cases, all 25 selected type graphs and the complete changed gate, full build, and fresh independent P0–P2 review. Targeted tests took 156.87 seconds, changed checks 1160.42 seconds, and the build 629.69 seconds. These are observed command costs, not controlled performance comparisons. The first CI's missing-source fixtures and test-ordering failures are corrected.

The hot-path regression observed 100 full-row reads before the correction and none after. Changed-revision predicates still parse JSON inside SQLite; a separate synthetic 8 MiB slow-path probe averaged 4.07 ms. Strict JSON and duplicate protected-key cases are covered. Four actual-preparer cells produce identical before/after results for the existing physical-key contract.

Earlier source-binding and authority-boundary proof is retained; overlapping groups are not summed. Tests use isolated SQLite/Git and mocked tunnels, not an external live provider or deployed cloud worker. The build's nonfatal UI gzip warning remains outside this change. Native review, hosted proof verification, and landing completed at `eacbd1d92afb579876b28890e1b66bc23905fd62`.

The refreshed head `f6318a53ca51d6ae4088a8b5ead46ed14ffa3133` aligns the same edit stream onto main `4d1c5d19ecc893ecef7b52cf7b3be002c794e770`. All 45 changed paths are retained; 40 postimages are byte-identical, and five incorporate upstream context. Fresh independent P0–P2 review confirms the guard still uses uncached before/after revision probes. No tests, build, or install were run locally on this refreshed head; earlier execution remains attributed to `774c`. [Fresh exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35929615799) passed in its first attempt, testing merge `ee1b7eaef1cb43fc0231f3600458d072b35b92c3` of this head with main `e9f7ff6814207fe06d342a214382731b51067903`. No recovery-PR CI rerun was used.

The prior [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35925563077) failed in a Skill Workshop fixture whose fake August clock overflowed a lease timer. The tested merge omitted its main parent’s immediate successor, [the fixture-clock fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/764c9331a31b4b87bdc06b95f39c6870c5aca2f3). The retained log explicitly shows each overflowing delay becoming 1 ms. This refresh includes that existing fix without changing production lease behavior.
